notes: Historical financial inputs are taken from Paycom’s FY2025 and FY2024 Form 10-K filings. Revenue and EBIT use total revenues and operating income, respectively; D&A uses depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement; capex uses cash purchases of property and equipment. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))

NWC construction (for all historical years and base/bull/bear via intensity): NWC = (Current assets before funds held for clients) − (Current liabilities before client funds obligation). This excludes client-float-related balance sheet items to better reflect operating working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))

Base-case forecast driver assumptions are anchored to FY2026 guidance growth (6%–7% YoY) and then taper; EBIT margin, D&A%, capex%, and NWC% are modeled as slowly converging ratios rather than volatile step changes. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

Known gaps/overrides: comps forward EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E NTM were not reliably captured from primary/high-quality sources in this run (set to null). WACC is an assumption (not sourced from filings). Terminal exit EBITDA multiple is null because the terminal_method is Gordon growth. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

catalysts: Revisions to FY2026 guidance (or stronger-than-guided recurring and other revenue growth) could imply upside to the base-case revenue chain. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

Client retention durability (highlighted as 91% in FY2025 commentary) and continued automation/AI adoption could support sustained gross retention and expansion. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

Capital returns (dividends/repurchases) and ongoing net cash position could improve equity valuation support if operating performance holds. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))
company_overview: Paycom is a cloud-based human capital management software company providing payroll, talent, and HR management applications with recurring revenue characteristics. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

In 2025, Paycom reported full-year total revenues of $2.052 billion and highlighted strong client retention to 91%. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

Paycom’s platform includes recent AI-driven product initiatives (e.g., IWant™) designed to simplify end-user workflows. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))
current_context: FY2026 guidance: total revenue range $2.175 billion to $2.195 billion (6% to 7% YoY), with recurring and other revenue growth of 7% to 8% YoY. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

FY2025 delivered $2.0517 billion of total revenues (+9.0% YoY) and ended the year with $370.0 million cash and total debt of $0. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))
Stock price snapshot as of the market close prior to 2026-03-21: $124.82.
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue trajectory is anchored to FY2026 guidance (6%–7% growth) and then tapers to low-to-mid single digits as the model reaches a mature run-rate. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

EBIT margin assumption moves toward a normalized level by 2030, consistent with the company’s scaling economics while recognizing recent EBIT volatility in historical results. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))

D&A and capex intensity are tied to historical depreciation and cash capital expenditures (purchases of property and equipment), with capex normalized below the 2025 spike. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))

Working capital intensity is modeled using a Paycom-consistent NWC definition that excludes client funds held and related client funds obligation, reducing distortions from payroll-related float. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Revenue growth may underperform if customer churn increases or if implementations do not scale as expected. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))

Operating margin could compress if operating expense growth (including R&D) outpaces revenue growth. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))
Working-capital dynamics could deviate from the modeled NWC intensity if deferred revenue timing or payroll-related flows change materially.

presentation.subtitle: DCF Input Package | Paycom (PAYC)
valuation_summary: DCF base-case is constructed from primary financial statement inputs (revenue, operating income/EBIT, depreciation & amortization, cash capex, and NWC) rather than from blended third-party estimates. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001590955/000119312526059372/payc-20251231.htm))

Terminal value uses a Gordon growth approach (terminal_growth = 0.025) to avoid imposing a potentially unstable terminal EV/EBITDA exit multiple where forward peer multiple data is not pulled. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/761236765/files/doc_news/Paycom-Software-Inc--Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Year-End-2025-Results-2026.pdf))
Scenario analysis provides a structured sensitivity around growth, operating leverage, and the discount rate rather than altering multiple unrelated drivers.
